title: Scan rejects documented xs=None in PyNative mode
duplicate_search_queries: site:gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/issues Scan xs None length isinstance arg 2 must be a type tuple types union MindSpore
site:github.com/mindspore-ai/mindspore/issues Scan None length isinstance arg 2 must be a type tuple types union MindSpore
duplicate_search_result: No exact matching GitHub or Gitee issue found for ops.Scan rejecting xs=None with length in PyNative mode.
documentation_notes: MindSpore 2.9 local Scan docstring documents xs as Union[tuple, list, None], length as Union[int, None], CPU support, and pseudocode that replaces xs=None with [None] * length.
The same local source shows Scan.__call__ validating xs with validator.check_value_type("xs", xs, [list, tuple, None], "Scan"), which passes None instead of type(None) into isinstance.
Graph mode accepts xs=None with both Python int init and Tensor init and returns the expected length-three scan outputs.
List and tuple xs controls pass in both PyNative and Graph mode.
classification_notes: Not a numerical precision issue: the failing path is a Python TypeError before any numeric kernel result is produced.
Not a CPU unsupported issue: Scan documents CPU support, and the list/tuple xs controls pass on CPU.
The failure is localized to PyNative argument validation for xs=None; Graph mode and non-None xs controls demonstrate that the loop function and result structure are valid.
The observed TypeError is an internal validator programming error rather than a documented user-facing validation error.
